newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Inca artifacts recovered in Honduras.
newsitem.headline: Inca artifacts recovered in Honduras.

text.p: Honduran authorities have seized 24 Incan archeological artifacts from a Dutch Honduran that they plan to return to Peru, officials said on Tuesday.
Some of the pieces date to as early as 200 B.C., said Eduardo Villanueva, special prosecutor for archeological crimes.
The Inca empire was one of the great pre-Colombian civilizations in the Americas. The Incas settled in what is modern-day Peru as well as parts of Ecuador, Chile and Argentina.
"These pieces have a tremendous historical value, and in accordance with international treaties we have seized them and will return them to Peru," Villanueva told reporters.
The ceramic vases and clay animal figures were found in the Atlantic port city of Trujillo, about 180 miles (290 km) north of Tegucigalpa.
They had been in the possession of Norbert Bart, a Honduran of Dutch origin who inherited them from his grandfather, Pieter Mathias Ferninand, a Dutch citizen.
Authorities said they were investigating whether to charge Bart with any crime.
The Honduran Institute of Anthropology and History is guarding the pieces until they can be returned to Peru.
